audit.why: 52.95% over 1560 games against a dashless mage who has to stand in your Q arc to drain — the page's read (contested level 1, yours from 2 onward, skill window at 4-5) matches both the numbers and the kits.

audit.whatIsWrong: The level-6 and first-item spikes were both written around Demonic Ascension 'stacking' — spikes[1].text says to kill him 'before his Demonic Ascension fully stacks', and whys[5] claims your HP wall simply out-grows his output.
audit.why: Demonic Ascension has no stack timer. Riot's text: the form is indefinite as long as Swain drains enemy champions. So the spike is not a race against a ramp — it is a leash you break by leaving the 650-unit range or knocking him up. And Ravenous Flock permanently increases his max health, so your HP wall is not growing against a fixed target.
audit.corrected: Rewrote spikes[1].text, spikes[3].text, whys[4] and whys[5] around the drain leash, the 650 range and the flat 120-second cooldown.
sources: champ-data/_kits/swain.json R text, range 650, cd 120; passive text

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing on the page mentions healing reduction, and wants.you[2] recommends an MR shard as the answer to his sustain.
audit.why: Ravenous Flock heals Swain off soul fragments and converts them into permanent max health. Both _missing rules for this matchup point at the same thing: he sustains through chip, and resistances do not answer health he regains. Grievous Wounds timing is what decides extended trades.
audit.corrected: Rewrote wants.you[2] around anti-heal and folded the point into whys[5].

audit.whatIsWrong: No cooldown numbers for the two abilities the lane is played around.
audit.why: Nevermove is 12s at rank 1 and Demonic Ascension is a flat 120s at every rank — the second number is the whole reason winning one fight at 6 is worth so much.

edits.before: Unstoppable Onslaught closes the gap past his W bomb positioning; landing the charged Q before Demonic Ascension stacks ends the trade.
edits.after: Unstoppable Onslaught closes past his W positioning, and a knockup ends Demonic Ascension — the form lasts only while he drains a champion.

edits.before: Heartsteel HP compounding outpaces Swain's flat drain — his Ascension damage has no %HP mechanic, so your wall simply grows faster than his output.
edits.after: Heartsteel compounds faster than Ravenous Flock — but its fragments heal him and raise his max health for good, so Grievous Wounds decides this window.

edits.before: Unstoppable Onslaught closes the gap on a rootless Swain; use R to blow past his W bomb positioning and then land the charged Q stun before his Demonic Ascension fully stacks.
edits.after: Unstoppable Onslaught closes on a dashless Swain; blow past his W positioning, then land the charged Q — the knockup drops him out of Demonic Ascension's drain entirely.

edits.before: Swain's Demonic Ascension is his biggest threat window — if he lands his E root and drains while you are CCed, the sustained AOE healing swings the trade hard; always break the root before fighting.
edits.after: Demonic Ascension only persists while he keeps draining a champion, so a root into drain swings the trade hard — leave his 650 range or land the knockup and the form ends on its own.

edits.before: Build Heartsteel into MR shard so your HP wall out-grows his flat drain output and your zombie passive guarantees trading value even if he catches you low
edits.after: Buy Grievous Wounds before the extended fights — Ravenous Flock heals him through chip, and raw MR does nothing about health he simply regains

edits.before: Levels 4-5 are the genuine skill window. Swain's W has decent range and if he hits it, the slow lets him run down and land his E root for a Demonic Ascension trade — do not let him open with W into E. Walk unpredictably and keep minions between you and his E boomerang. At level 6 the matchup tips back hard: your Unstoppable Onslaught is an instant gap-closer that bypasses his W bomb positioning, and the follow-up charged Q knockup lands before his Ascension stacks enough to matter. If he activates Demonic Ascension during a trade, immediately use E to slow and keep distance or throw a charged Q to break his position — the drain requires him to stay in range and the knockup interrupts his cadence. He has no escape, so once you are on him at 6 the only way he survives is if Ascension is already stacked and you are already low.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 are the genuine skill window. Vision of Empire reaches far and if it lands, the slow lets him run you down into an E root for the drain — do not let him open W into E. Walk unpredictably and keep minions between you and Nevermove, which roots on the return arc, not the throw. At level 6 the matchup tips back hard: Unstoppable Onslaught bypasses his W positioning and the follow-up knockup lands before the drain does anything. Demonic Ascension only lasts while he is draining a champion inside 650 units, so E-slow him and walk out, or knock him up, and the form drops on its own. It is a flat 120 seconds at every rank, so one won fight at 6 buys you two minutes of a lane where he has no answer at all.
